title: Drift velocity of electrons in a wire connected to a battery with internal resistance
summary: A 100 m wire across a 2 V battery with 1 ohm internal resistance: the current appears at once, but each electron drifts at only 0.208 mm/s. R = 1 ohm, I = 1 A, n = 6e28 m^-3, vd = I/(neA) = 0.208 mm/s - option C.
subject: Physics
topic: Drift velocity of electrons in a wire on a battery with internal resistance - a large current from a slow drift
subtopics: Resistance from conductivity: R = L/(sigma A)
EMF and internal resistance: I = eps/(R + r); terminal voltage across the wire
Free-electron density from density, molar mass and Avogadro's number
Drift velocity and current: I = n e A vd; J = sigma E = n e vd
concepts: R = 100 / (2e8 x 0.5e-6) = 1 ohm; I = 2/(1 + 1) = 1 A - the wire gets only 1 V of the 2 V
n = rho NA / M = 6.35e3 x 6e23 / 63.5e-3 = 6e28 m^-3 (one free electron per atom)
vd = I/(n e A) = 1/4800 m/s = 0.208 mm/s - option C; the field route sigma E/(ne) with E = 0.01 V/m agrees
The current appears at once because the field is set up through the whole wire; each electron drifts so slowly it would need 5.6 days to travel 100 m
Traps: ignoring r gives 0.417 mm/s (no option); grams or mm^2 left unconverted give answers off by 1000
formulas: vd = sigma E/(n e), E = V/L

methods: MathonGo solution (their Q19 = Physics Q.1) read first as the conceptual reference; its answer (C) agrees
Independent solve: R = 1 ohm, I = 1 A, n = 6e28 m^-3, vd = 1/4800 m/s = 0.208 mm/s
Circuit route in exact fractions: vd = I/(n e A) = 1/4800 m/s
Field route in exact fractions: V = IR = 1 V, E = 0.01 V/m, vd = sigma E/(n e) - equal to the circuit route
Collision Monte Carlo (NCERT picture): free times exponential with tau = m sigma/(n e^2); the time-averaged velocity equals eE tau/m = vd within 1%
Traps and options: r = 0 gives 0.417 (no option); options A, B, D are 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 of the answer
